## Review

_Congratulations, you've completed this exercise and learned how to create a digital collection website with CollectionBuilder!_ 🎉

<img src="https://octodex.github.com/images/jetpacktocat.png" alt="celebrate" width=200 align=right>

Here's a recap of your accomplishments:

- ✅ **Set up a development environment** in GitHub Codespaces
- ✅ **Learned the Git workflow** (add, commit, push)
- ✅ **Explored CSV metadata** and how it drives digital collections
- ✅ **Edited collection metadata** to customize items
- ✅ **Configured Jekyll** to use your metadata
- ✅ **Built and previewed** your collection locally with Ruby and Bundle
- ✅ **Customized content** using Markdown
- ✅ **Deployed to GitHub Pages** for free public hosting

Your digital collection is now live on the web! 🌐

### Technical Skills Learned

Through this tutorial, you've gained foundational skills in:

- **Git version control**: Tracking changes, committing, and pushing
- **GitHub Codespaces**: Cloud-based development environments
- **Command-line tools**: Terminal navigation and commands
- **Jekyll & Ruby**: Static site generation with bundle and Jekyll
- **Markdown**: Simple markup for formatted content
- **CSV data**: Structured metadata for collections
- **GitHub Pages**: Static site hosting and deployment

### What's next?

- **Customize your collection**: Add more items to your CSV, customize the theme in `_data/theme.yml`, or modify page layouts
- **Learn more about CollectionBuilder**: Explore the [CollectionBuilder documentation](https://collectionbuilder.github.io/cb-docs/)
- **Join the community**: Ask questions in the [CollectionBuilder Discussion Forum](https://github.com/CollectionBuilder/collectionbuilder.github.io/discussions)
- **Try advanced features**: Add compound objects, customize visualizations, or integrate with digital asset management systems
- **Build your own collection**: Apply what you've learned to create a collection from your own materials!
